full_judgment:
Mr. Siddiqur Rahman Miah, J: This revisional application under section 115(4) of the Code of Civil Procedure at the instance of the plaintiff opposite party is directed against the judgment and order dated 27.11.2005 passed by the learned District Judge, Narayangonj, in Civil Miscellaneous Case No. 111 of 2005 arising out of Money suit No. 03 of 2004 transferring the same from the court of Joint District Judge, First court, to the Joint District Judge, 2nd Court, Narayangonj. 

 5. It is further stated on behalf of the opposite parties that Civil Miscellaneous Case No. 111 of 2005 under section 24 of the Code of Civil Procedure was filed in the court of the learned District Judge, Narayangonj, for transferring the money suit No. 03 of 2004 from the Court of the Joint District Judge, first court, Narayangonj. The learned District Judge passed order No. 111 of 27.11.2005 and allowed the application and transferred the Money Suit No. 03 of 2004 to the Court of the learned Joint District Judge, 2nd court, Narayangonj from the court of the learned Joint District Judge, First court, Narayangonj. 

 9. Now let us see law regarding the transfer of case which is enumerated in section 24 of the Code of Civil Procedure: 

 (2) Where any suit or proceeding has been transferred or withdrawn under section (1) the court which thereafter tries such suit may subject to any special directions in the case of any order of transfer, either retry it or proceed from the point at which it was transferred or withdrawn. 

 24A—(1) Where any suit is transferred under section 22, or any suit, appeal or other proceeding is transferred or withdrawn under sub-section (1) of section 24 on the application of a party, the court ordering the transfer or withdrawal shall fix a date for appearance of the parties before itself, if the suit, appeal or other proceeding is to be tried or disposed of by itself, or before the Court to which the case is so transferred. 

 10. As general rule, a plaintiff as arbiter lit is or do minus lit is has a right to choose his own forum where there is more than one court in which the suit can be filed. But the said right is controlled by the power vested in the superior courts to transfer a case pending in one inferior court to another or to withdraw the case to itself for hearing and disposal. 

 11. Before transfer is ordered, two conditional conditions must be satisfied namely; (i) the application must be made at the earliest possible opportunity and in all cases where issues are settled, at or before the settlement of issues; and (ii) notice must j he given to the other side. The provision as 'to notice is mandatory. Such notice may be given by the party making an application or by the court. 

 12. The court can pass such order if it is satisfied that such an order is "expedient in the ends of justice." In the light of the decision of the apex Courts of this sub-continent, we decided grounds for transfer and not transfer of the cases. The following have been held to the sufficient grounds for transfer: (i) reasonable apprehension in the mind of the litigant that he might not get justice in the court in which the suit is pending. (ii) to avoid multiplicity of proceedings or conflicting decisions, (iii) where the judge is interested in one party or biased against the other (iv) were common questions of fact and law arise between the parties in two suits (v) on the ground of balance of convenience e.g. where the property is situated or parties reside; or the account books are kept etc. (vi) where two persons have filed suits against each other in deferent courts on the same cause of action (vii) to avoid delay and unnecessary expenses (viii) where important questions of law are involved or considerable section of public is interested in the litigation (ix) to prevent abuse of the process of court; 

 13. The following, on the other hand, have been held not to be sufficient grounds for transfer: (i) mere fact that the opposite party is a man of influence in the locality, (ii) mere fact that the court.is situated at a long distance from the place of the residence of the applicant (iii) mere fact that the presiding officer belongs to a community rival to that of the applicant (iv) mere that the judge has decided a similar point in a previous case. (v) mere balance of convenience to the applicant (vi) refusal to grant adjournment (vii) prejudice of a Judge against party's pleader not likely to affect the party (viii) Judge making adverse remarks regarding merits of the case; (ix) allegation of apprehension against fair trail without furnishing particulars (x) one counsel losing temper and using un-parliamentary language, the judge ordering adjournment etc. 

 14. Now let us see as to whether the facts and circumstances of the case fit for transfer of the instant suit. 

 16. It appears from the order sheet that as per the order No. 68 A dated 14.10.2004 of the learned Joint District Judge the suit being No. 03 of 2004 was transferred to the court of first Joint District Judge previously. The suit at argument stage. The learned Joint District Judge asked staff to inform the matter to the parties Concerned and also fixed the case on 28.11.2004 for hearing argument. The plaintiff prayed for time on 24.11.2004 and the court allowed the same fixing 28.11.2004 for hearing argument. The plaintiff, Janata Bank, being aggrieved by the order dated 28.11.2004 presumed that he will not get fair justice from that court. So the Bank as petitioner filed application on 29.11.2004 before the learned District Judge under section 24 of the Code of Civil Procedure for transferring the suit from the first Joint District Judge on the ground that he will not get justice in that court. The learned District Judge after hearing passed impugned judgment and order on 27.11.2005 transferring the suit from first court to 2nd court of Joint District Judge made a comment that the learned joint District Judge without hearing the case fixed suit for argument and such view of the learned District Judge is beyond the record. The learned District Judge made a comment that the learned Joint District without going through the facts of the case and relevant order sheet passed the impugned order on irrelevant ground. In view of the above legal position there is no valid ground for transferring the suit and moreover the learned District Judge also did not apply his judicial mind in passing the impugned order. In the instant case, the contention of the opposite parties is that they filed an application for transfer under section 24 of the Code of Civil Procedure on suspicion that they would not get fair justice from the learned Joint District Judge, first court, Nnrayangonj but suspicion unless supported by particular and solid materials cannot he a ground for transfer of a case. Mere inconvenience of one party cannot be a ground for transfer of a case. The apprehension must appear to the court to be reasonable, genuine and justifiable. Power of transfer of a case cannot be exercised on hypersensitive or trivial grounds or mini grievances. 

 18. in view of the facts and circumstances of the case and law bear the matter we find merit in the Rule which must succeed. 

 19. In the result, the Rule is made absolute without any order as to costs. The impugned judgment and order dated 27.11.2005 passed by the learned District Judge, Narayangonj in civil Miscellaneous Case No.111 of 2005 is set aside and the learned Joint District Judge, First Court, Narayangonj is directed to proceed with the suit in accordance with law.
